summary: R-3 special design lookout on Mount Withington in the Cibola National Forest, Socorro County; present cab 1952, first cupola 1934; NHLR-registered 2006.

facts.design: Special R-3 design cab with a slightly sloped gable roof on a concrete block base; a catwalk was added later
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Cibola National Forest (Magdalena Ranger District as cooperator)

events.note: First lookout on the site: a D-6 cupola that served 18 years
Present R-3 station replaced the 1934 cupola; the FFLA report says the lookout was erected in 1952
Evaluated for NRHP under the thematic nomination Lookouts of the Southwest Region; not eligible due to age
Registered April 30, 2006 as US 669, NM 23; nominated by Dave Lorenz

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1952 is the present station. The register says the first lookout on the site was a D-6 cupola built in 1934 and replaced in 1952; the 2020 report gives only 1952.

sources.title: Travel guide to the top of Mount Withington in New Mexico

notes_for_editor: The register and the FFLA 2020 report agree on the 1952 station. The 1934 cupola appears only in the NHLR text. No staffing, fire or rental listing was found; the 2020 report does not mark the lookout for the cabin rental program. Road details come from a travel guide, not a Forest Service page, so the closure dates (Oct 1 to May 15) should be checked before anyone relies on them. drive_up true refers to the summit road, which the guide describes as seasonal and 4x4-only. The record's built 1952 is right for the present station and is left unchanged; no correction filed. Not verified: current condition, and whether the cab is open to visitors.
